extracted.intended_audience: researchers, research-integrity professionals, journalists and the general scientific community interested in retractions and misconduct
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluating alleged scientific misconduct in a biomedical research article (animal study), including factual accuracy, data integrity, authorship responsibility, and institutional/journal responses. Focuses on criteria used by institutions and ethics boards to determine misconduct and appropriate remedies (e.g., retraction, sanctions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation of results inconsistent with research outcome (scientific misconduct)
rubrics_metrics.description: “It is therefore, in the Expert Group’s view, conclusively established that the presentation of the results in the article is inconsistent with the outcome of the research that was conducted, which is scientific misconduct.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the key legal/ethical standard used by the Expert Group: if the way results are presented in the paper does not reflect what was actually observed, that constitutes scientific misconduct. Examples given include reported successes that were not achieved and conclusions that do not follow from the underlying data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy of reported animal outcomes and welfare
rubrics_metrics.description: The report notes that claims (e.g., all animals survived 14 days; transplanted animals gained more weight) were contradicted by the raw data: “The rats … showed very significant weight loss, which would not have been the case if the experiment had been a success.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors must accurately report animal outcomes and welfare; if animals deteriorated (significant weight loss, poor condition), this undermines claimed successes and may indicate misconduct. Ethical implication: experiments showing severe deterioration should have been stopped.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate stopping of experiments when animals deteriorate
rubrics_metrics.description: “In addition, the rats lost so much weight and deteriorated so much in condition that the experiment should have been stopped.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigators are expected to halt experiments when humane/ethical endpoints are met. Continuing despite severe deterioration is an ethical breach and supports findings of misleading or irresponsible conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy and consistency of figures/images with raw data
rubrics_metrics.description: “The pictures and figures that reportedly demonstrate the success of the experiment are also incorrect and misleading in several places. The raw data that the Expert Group has had access to is not always consistent with the figures in the article, which leads to incorrect conclusions…”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Figures and images in a manuscript must faithfully represent the underlying raw data. Inconsistencies between raw data and presented figures that alter interpretation are grounds for finding misleading presentation or misconduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correct interpretation and use of references (not misleading ethical review committees)
rubrics_metrics.description: “The article also contains a number of references which have resulted in incorrect interpretations, thereby misleading the ethical committee on animal research.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References must be used accurately; misrepresenting prior work or citing in ways that produce incorrect interpretations (especially those that could influence ethical review decisions) is a serious issue for research integrity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author responsibility tied to insight/overview of the project
rubrics_metrics.description: KI: “Karolinska Institutet finds that Paolo Macchiarini and three of the co-authors had insight into and an overview of the process, either in its entirety or in large part, and are thus to be found guilty of scientific misconduct. The remaining authors contributed in ways that are not judged to constitute misconduct, nor were they in a position to have had insight into or an overview of the whole project.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutions evaluate authors’ level of involvement and oversight; those with overall insight/overview (typically senior authors) may be held accountable for misconduct, while contributors with limited, constrained roles may not be held to the same standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of dependency and mitigating circumstances for junior researchers
rubrics_metrics.description: KI explained that “the two junior researchers were in a position of dependency towards their more senior colleagues … their circumstances must be considered mitigating. They have therefore been issued with a caution.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigations often weigh power dynamics and dependency: junior researchers under pressure from seniors may receive lighter sanctions or cautions rather than full penalties; this affects determinations of culpability and sanctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional oversight and active follow-up to ensure good research practice
rubrics_metrics.description: “The responsible department head at Karolinska Institutet shall in the next two years … actively follow up and support the research they conduct at Karolinska Institutet to ensure that the research is conducted in accordance with good research practice.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutions should impose active monitoring and mentorship requirements after misconduct findings to ensure future compliance with good research practice; departmental responsibility is a remediation criterion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Journal procedures: expression of concern and retraction requests after institutional findings
rubrics_metrics.description: The paper “has already been flagged with an expression of concern” and KI “is contacting the journal to request a retraction of the paper.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When an institution finds misconduct, appropriate journal actions include flagging with an expression of concern and requesting retraction where warranted. The presence of an EOC and a formal retraction request are part of the remediation/communication process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Re-examination of earlier clearances in light of new evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Although Macchiarini was “initially cleared of misconduct in the 2014 paper … in 2015,” KI reopened the investigation after new documentaries raised allegations and the investigators took a second look.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigative conclusions may be revisited if new evidence emerges; earlier clearances are not necessarily final and institutions may reopen cases to reassess the evidence and findings.
